newsitem.title: USA: GPU has few problems with 100 pct choice.
newsitem.headline: GPU has few problems with 100 pct choice.

text.p: GPU Inc's New Jersey operations have no problem with going immediately to 100 percent customer choice of power supplier the needed administrative structure is ready, Elizabeth Ard, vice president of corporate affairs for the state, said Tuesday.
In its electric industry restructuring filing with the state Board of Public Utilities, GPU supported acceptance of the board's proposal to phase in customer choice over three years.

In its April restructuring order, the board proposed that users of 10 percent of demand be allowed to select energy suppliers as of October 1998, an additional 10 percent in January 1999, a 15 percent allowance in both April and October of 1999, and a 25 percent increment in both April and July of 2000.

Public Service Enterprise Group Inc said its Public Service Electric & Gas Co subsidiary proposed 100 percent customer choice of power suppliers on starting January 1, 1999, in Tuesday's filing with state regulators.
If the administrative structure "is ready, we have not problem with" this, Ard said in a telephone interview.

She was joined by Director of Rates/New Jersey Ike Fillippone who said GPU's proposal to recognize capacity credits once a capacity market exited in addition to trading in electricity itself amounted to "yes, but."

He said the company is prepared to recognize capacity credits once they have a value, but would "true-up (the recognized credits) to actual capacity at the end of the year." ((-- New York Newsdesk 212 859-1610))
